root_cause.text: In `f2fs`’s `check_swap_activate()`, when an unaligned extent causes `nr_pblocks` to become zero after rounding to section size, the code incorrectly sets `last_extent = true` and migrates all remaining blocks, then fails to re‑lookup the block mapping (because the retry is conditioned on `!last_extent`), leaving subsequent extents unmapped and causing swap writes to target wrong physical blocks.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and patch diff highlight the problematic logic: `if (!nr_pblocks) { nr_pblocks = last_lblock - cur_lblock; last_extent = true; }` followed by `if (!last_extent) goto retry;`. The patch fixes this by moving `last_extent` outside the loop, adding `!last_extent` as a guard to the alignment check, and unconditionally retrying after migration.

Declares the flag that controls retry logic. This flag is later set to true incorrectly on zero nr_pblocks, preventing re-lookup.
The rounding operation can turn a non-zero nr_pblocks into zero if the original value is fractional relative to section size, leading to the erroneous last_extent = true setting.

This conditional directly gates the retry of block mapping lookup. When last_extent is incorrectly set to true, the retry is skipped, leaving subsequent extents unmapped and causing swap writes to target wrong physical blocks.

When last_extent is incorrectly set to true (due to zero nr_pblocks after rounding), this condition fails, and the retry is skipped, leaving subsequent extents unmapped and causing swap writes to target wrong physical blocks.

This goto is the actual retry action. It is only reached when !last_extent is true. When last_extent is incorrectly true, this retry is bypassed, which is the core control-flow error that prevents re-lookup of block mappings.
